full_judgment:
Md Shamsul Huda J: One Alhaj Mokbul Hossain, son of Late Mohammad Ali preferred an appeal under section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 challenging the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 6-5-2008 passed by the Special Judge, Court No. 9, Dhaka in Special Case No. 9 of 2008 arising out of Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 60(8)2007 convicting the convict petitioner and another under section 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 3 years and also convicting him under section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and to pay a fine of Taka 10 lac in default to suffer imprisonment for another one year more, along with an application for con-donation of delay in filing the Appeal. 

 2. The whole crux of the case is now before us, in short, is that the trial was held in absence of the appellant petitioner during last so-called Care Taker Government upon a case being initiated by the Anti-Corruption Commission and he was convicted and sentenced as stated above. After the change of the said regime the appellant Alhaj Mokbul Hossain preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5294 of 2009 before this Court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The application was moved along with some other applications preferred by some other convicts before a Division Bench of this Court. The Bench having been divided in their opinion those matters were referred to the Hon'ble Chief Justice who referred the matter to Mr Justice Imman Ali for disposal. After hearing the parties Mr Justice Imman Ali by his order dated 23rd day of May, 2009 directed all the petitioners of the respective cases to surrender before the concerned Court who passed the judgment and order of conviction and sentence. Accordingly the appellant surrendered before Mr Muzammel Hossain, Special Judge, Court No. 9 (in-charge), Dhaka on 20-9-2010 with an application for bail along with a certified copy of the order dated 15-9-2008 passed by Mr Justice Imman Ali in Writ Petition No. 6606 of 2008. 

 3. The learned Special Judge passed an elaborate order stating that the petitioner in compliance with the order of the High Court Division passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 5294 of 2009 appeared before him and on scrutiny of record he found that the appellant along with his wife Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam were convicted in this case vide judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 6-5-2008. But in pursuance of Writ Petition No. 6606 of 2008 filed by Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam, the High Court Division vide order dated 15-9-2008 stayed further operation of the judgment and order dated 6-5-2008 passed by the Special Judge, Court No. 9, Dhaka in Special Case No. 9 of 2008 for a period of 3(three) months which was extended time to time and lastly it was extended on 24-1-2010 by a Division Bench of this Court for a period of 6(six) months from the date of expiry. In the above circumstances since High Court Division has stayed operation of entire judgment and order of the case there lies no scope on the part of this Court to consider the surrender of the accused till expiry of the said order of the Hon'ble High Court Division. Therefore, let the petition be kept with the record. With this order the learned Special Judge-in-charge dis-posed of the surrender application of the appellant herein. 

 7. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that in view of the above fact that this appellant was tried in absentia and convicted as stated above during the last so-called Care Taker Government while abnormal situation was prevailing in this country, specially the political leaders including two former Prime Ministers were arrested and harassed and present appellant being a former Member of Parliament and renowned businessman, social worker and political leader, could not remain in the country and as a result he could not face the trial. In short in can be said that the appellant was compelled to leave his homeland to save his prestige, dignity and political image, as the situation was beyond his control. The aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5294 of 2009 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was summarily disposed of by a learned Third Judge of this Court directing him to surrender before the Court below. Accordingly, in pursuance of the order of this Court he surrendered before the Court below, but unfortunately the learned Special Judge in-charge without applying his judicial mind refused to accept the surrender. On the other hand he has violated the order of a competent bench of the High Court Division, on a mere plea that there is a stay order in respect of the entire judgment in a writ petition preferred by his wife (co-accused) wherein this appellant was not a party at all. Furthermore, the learned Special Judge has forgotten that he is subordinate to the High Court Division and this appellant surrendered before him on the basis of a direction of the High Court Division. It was his bounden duty to accept his surrender, but he failed. On this score Mr Abdul Matin Khasru argued that for the fault of the Court below a citizen of the country cannot suffer and pressed hard to pass an appropriate order on the application for condonation of delay and to admit the appeal. In view of the above facts, circumstances and documentary proves that the appellant has voluntarily surrendered before the Court below the appellant cannot be termed as fugitive, so there is no bar to admit the appeal. 

 8. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission submits that on perusal of the order of the learned Special Judge-in-charge it appears to him that whole anomaly has been created by the said Special Judge in not accepting the surrender of the appellant herein and also by ignoring the lawful order of the High Court Division, due to his ignorance of law. But since the said order of the High Court Division in the aforesaid writ petition is in force the appellant may be further directed to appear before the learned Special Judge and also to direct the Special Judge to accept his surrender. In respect of definition of "fugitive" Mr Khan very sincerely submits that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case he completely agrees with Mr Khasru, the learned Advocate for the appellant and the appellant cannot be termed as "fugitive" at any point of time. Mr Khan further, submits that the learned Special Judge could refer the matter for clarification to the High Court Division through the Registrar, keeping the surrender application pending. Lastly he submits that in view of the above fact this Court can keep the appeal pending and direct the appellant to surrender before the Court below. 

 9. In this regard he referred a decision reported in 15 BLC (AD) 45 and another unreported case being Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 411 of 2009, judgment passed on 14-3-2010 wherein it has been held that, "The petitioner is a fugitive from justice when he moved the petition and obtained the rule nisi. This Court repeatedly argued that a fugitive from justice is not entitled to obtain .a judicial order defying the process of the Court. When a person wants to seek remedy from a Court of Law, he is required to submit to the due process of the Court and unless he surrenders to the jurisdiction of the Court, the Court will not pass any order in his aid. 

 10. In view of the above, the learned Judges of the High Court Division illegally entertained the writ petition and stayed further proceedings of the case." 

 11. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Counsel submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the present case the appellant cannot be termed as "fugitive" from justice. In short, he submitted that the wrong done by the learned Special Sessions Judge-in-charge for which the appellant should not suffer. If the appellant is not fugitive this Court has power to accept his prayer. But for maintaining decorum and long standing practice of this Court the appellant may be further directed to surrender before the Court concerned and the said Court is to be directed to accept his surrender and proceed in accordance with law, keeping the appeal stand over for a certain period in this Court. 

 13. Mr Khan Saifur Rahman, learned Counsel also submitted that in the given facts and circumstances of the case the appellant cannot termed as "fugitive" from justice and a person who is not fugitive from justice he can seek redress before this Court, as soon as he Surrendered before the Court below as directed by the High Court Division he has ceased to be "fugitive". He further submitted that this Court can exercise power under Sub-section 1 and 2 of section 426 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and suspend the execution of the impugned judgment and in turn this Court can admit the appeal. 

 15. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, learned Advocate for the appellant most strenuously argued that appeal is a right of a convict, which cannot be withheld for the fault, or mistake of the Court below. The present appellant com-plied the order of this Court and submitted himself to the process of law. In view of the above fact he cannot be thrown out of justice considering him fugitive. In support of his sub-mission he referred a case reported in 58 DLR 106, Md Jahangir Hossain Howlader vs CMM, Dhaka wherein it has been held that: 

 "In the case in hand, just a first information report was filed and warrant of arrest was yet to be issued by the Magistrate. By filing the writ petition, the petitioner has been before this Court and therefore, he cannot be termed a fugitive from justice." 

 16. In the meantime, the learned Attorney-General appeared and addressed the Court. He also conceded to the contention of the learned Senior Advocate of the Bar and submitted that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the present situation the present appellant cannot be treated as "fugitive" but to maintain the long standing practice of this Court he may be directed to surrender before the Court below and obtain a power being executed by him after surrender, being attested by the Officer-in-charge of the Police Court, keeping the appeal of the appellant pending before this Court. 

 "It is true that the Sessions Judge was not competent to grant such bail under section 426 of the Code of Criminal Procedure since the sentence was in excess of one year. The order was therefore, illegal but the fact remains that the appellants submitted themselves to the sentence passed and obtained an interim order of bail in their favour albeit wrongly. In the facts of the case it will be less than charitable to attribute to the appellants that they were 'fugitive from law'. There was nothing in their conduct to show that they were running away from the jurisdiction of the Court or avoiding its process. Since, however, the appellants were not covered by a legal order of interim bail, the proper order the learned Judge ought to have passed and which is always usually passed in such cases was to direct the appellants to surrender within a certain time before taking up the petition of appeal for hearing". 

 18. The fact of the case in hand and the fact of the aforesaid cited case is different no doubt, but the principle settled in respect of the term "fugitive from law" is very much applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 19. By the change of the democratic government, an autocratic power had changed the situation of the country radically, as a result a series of cases were decided in the absence of the accused persons, mainly the political leaders and the businessmen of this country which cannot be denied. Since there was no constitutional Government in the country a series of cases were tried in absentia and subsequently some of them directly appeared before this Court and preferred application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and some writ petitions and obtained stay order of the conviction and sentence, although they were fugitive from justice at that time. A bunch of cases of this nature have been decided by our Appellate Division and discouraged that practice. It has been held in a case of ACC vs Dr HBM Iqbal Alamgir by our Appellate Division reported in 15 BLC (AD) 44. 

 Admittedly, the writ petitioner was convicted in absentia by the judgment and order dated 13 March, 2008 by the Special Judge, First Court, Dhaka. Naturally, the learned Special Judge issued Warrant for the execution of the sentence under section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the time of delivery of judgment, and the writ petitioner moved the petition on 17th September, 2008 when there was warrant for the execution of the sentence. It is not understood in such backdrop of the case, how the learned Judges of the Division Bench could even entertain the writ petition on behalf of a fugitive from justice, ignoring the long settled principle being followed by the Courts? If this process is allowed, the fugitives from justice either convicted or not will be emboldened and despite processes have been issued, they will defy the processes of the Courts and in such cases, the administration of criminal justice will be crumpled. A convict who seeks the interference of the sovereign to obtain revision of a judicial order must submit to the Court instead of engaging himself in setting that judicial order at naught. It is well settled that when a person seeks remedy from a Court of law, either in writ jurisdiction or criminal appellate, revision-al or miscellaneous jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure he ought to submit to the due process of justice. Let it be made clear to him, if it is not already known that the Court would not act in aid of an accused person who is a fugitive from law and justice." 

 20. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate in course of his submission referred an unreported case of the Appellate Division, Anti-Corruption Commission vs ATM Nazimzullah Chowdhury in Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 411 of 2009, judgment and order passed on 14-3-2010 wherein it has been held that, 

 "The petitioner is a fugitive from justice when he moved the petition and obtained the rule nisi. This Court repeatedly argued that a fugitive from justice is not entitled to obtain a judicial order defying the process of the Court. When a person wants to seek remedy from a Court of Law, he is required to submit to the due process of the Court and unless he surrendered to the jurisdiction of the Court, the Court will not pass any order in his aid. In view of the above, the learned Judges of the High Court Division illegally entertained the writ petition and stayed further proceedings of the case." 

 21. He further refers a case of. Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mahmud Hossain reported in 61 DLR (AD) 17 wherein it has been held that, "A man who seeks justice from the Court of law must come before the Court to agitate his grievance and must surrender first to the process of justice, otherwise he remains fugitive from justice and could not seek aid or assistance of the process of justice in order to claim right of audience."  23. We have brought the record of Writ Petition No. 6606 of 2008 and perused the same to satisfy ourselves for the ends of justice. It appears from the aforesaid case record that Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam, wife of Alhaj Mokbul Hossain was the sole writ petitioner in the aforesaid writ petition. The prayer portion of the writ petition is as follows: (B) Pending hearing of the Rule stay the judgment and order passed in Special Case No. 9 of 2008 before the Special Court No. 9 Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka dated 6-5-2008. 

 A Division Bench of this Court passed the following order in respect of the stay: "Pending hearing of the rule the operation of the judgment and order dated 6-5-2008 passed in Special Case No. 9 of 2008 by the Special Judge, Court No. 9, Dhaka, be stayed for a period of 3(three) months from date." 

 25. Though we are not entitled to pass any comment in respect of an order passed by another Bench of this Court in a writ petition, but on perusal of case record we want to add our opinion here that the learned members of the Bar should be cautious in drafting the applications  for writ petition or any matter. Its prayer portion should be in correct form, because in the aforesaid case 2 persons were convicted, one is writ petitioner Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam and another is Alhaj Mokbul Hossain. Said Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam is the sole petitioner in the aforesaid Writ Petition No. 6606 of 2008 but in the prayer portion the learned Advocate for the writ petitioner made a prayer to stay the impugned judgment which is not proper. He ought to have prayed to stay the impugned judgment in respect of his client i.e. Mrs Golam Fatima Tahera Khanam. 

 27. However, this type of practice of granting stay order either in writ petition or in 561A matter has been highly criticized and discouraged by our Appellate Division in numbers of cases amongst which we have referred some of the decisions. 

 28. In this regard we are inclined to record our opinion that when a Judge passes any judicial order he must be respectful to its own oath i.e. not to fear or favour anybody. It must be in accordance with law only. Nobody is above the law, but in the recent .past.in some particular cases stay orders/bail orders were passed in favour of the absconders, who made the image of this Court subject matter of criticism even by a layman. 

 29. In this regard we may refer to a case of Dr Ahmed Sharif vs State reported in 1997 BLD 235 = 49 DLR 100 wherein in has been held by his Lordships Mr AKM Sadeque sitting with Mr Justice KM Hasan (as his Lordship then was), that, "The petitioner was a Professor of Dhaka University and is one of the intellectuals of this country but this does not absolve him of the responsibility of appearing before a Court and asking for bail which, is due to him in the facts and circumstances of the case." In this 'case their Lordships referred the case of AK Khan vs Chairman, Second Labour Court of East Pakistan reported in 25 DLR 192 wherein it has been held that, 

 31. In the case in hand the fact is other-wise. It is a consensus opinion of the Bar that Alhaj Mokbul Hossain is not fugitive from justice. But to maintain the long standing practice of this Court and showing respect to the decisions of the Appellate Division we have considered the position of the appellant petitioner at this stage and we agree with the learned Attorney-General and other members of the Bar that the ends of justice will be met, if we modify the order dated 20-4-2010 passed by the learned Special Judge-in-charge, Specials Court No. 9, Dhaka and direct the appellant petitioner to appear before him and also direct the learned Special Judge-on-charge, Special Court No. 9, Dhaka to accept his surrender and to proceed in accordance with law.
